To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a confirmation theory can be used to improve an incorrect domain theory; (2) a confirmation theory is also useful for improving an inconsistent domain theory; (3) an explicit representation of strategy knowledge is necessary for improving an inconsistent or incomplete domain theory; and (4) an explicit representation for the domain knowledge is also necessary for improving an incorrect domain theory.
we have developed a learning method for knowledge base refinement that can be used to improve a domain theory in a way that is both effective and efficient.

1) a declarative representation of the domain theory, 2) a representation of strategy knowledge that is separate from domain theory, and 3) an explicit connection to a confirmation theory are necessary to achieve significant knowledge base refinement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods for learning from examples in the domain of knowledge-based systems.
improving domain theories in the presence of incorrectness, inconsistency and incompleteness by using a confirmation theory and strategy knowledge to guide the refinement process.
the development of techniques for improving a domain theory that is incorrect, inconsistent, incomplete, or a combination of these pathologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown that it is possible to learn from a single example to improve an incorrect and inconsistent domain theory.

the knowledge base refinement techniques that we have developed have proven to be very effective at improving a domain theory in the three areas of incorrectness, inconsistency and incompleteness, as measured by the performance of the resulting system on a test set.
our approach to knowledge base refinement has been successful in a variety of applications, but the approach is still immature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the feasibility of using learning techniques to improve an incorrect, inconsistent, and incomplete domain theory.
we have demonstrated the utility of using the domain theory to guide the refinement process, and that we have developed techniques to handle a wide range of domain theory pathologes.
the use of explicit, modular, declarative representations for domain theories, domain theory pathologies, and domain theory improvement strategies is a very powerful approach to knowledge refinement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a declarative knowledge representation is essential to learning from failure.
it is possible to improve a knowledge base that is incorrect, inconsistent, incomplete, and even inconsistent and incomplete.

the explicit representation of domain theory and strategy knowledge is a powerful tool that allows us to reason about domain theory pathologies and to use a wide range of learning techniques to address them.
